title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
book_title: Chapter 3: The Plumbing of Margins — How Every ₹100 Flows Through Zydus

epigraph.quote: Revenue is vanity, EBITDA is sanity, and operating cash flow after working capital is reality.
epigraph.author: Institutional accounting proverb

web_blocks.html: Zydus operates three distinct go-to-market (GTM) models depending on the buyer. In North America, generics ship from Gujarat hubs (Moraiya, Ahmedabad SEZ, Jarod) to US distribution centers. Three buying consortia (Walgreens/AmerisourceBergen, CVS/Cardinal, McKesson/Walmart) control that channel, forcing steep gross-to-net rebates and annual price resets. By contrast, Sentynl's rare-disease drugs (Zokinvy, ZYCUBO) and Saroglitazar rely on a small specialty sales force. Patient-support hubs and specialty pharmacies handle direct payer reimbursement.

In India Formulations, thousands of medical reps call on cardiologists, hepatologists, and oncologists. CFAs, stockists, and retail pharmacies fulfill orders in a cash-generative, low-receivable model. Meanwhile, Consumer Wellness pairs Indian kirana and modern-trade reach with digital D2C fulfillment (Amazon UK/EU) via Comfort Click [10]. Amplitude Surgical sells orthopedic implants directly to European hospital groups [9].

web_blocks.takeaway: At peak FY26 gross margins (~73.1%), every ₹100 of sales yielded ₹31.22 of EBITDA and ₹18.87 of PAT—but working-capital absorption and capex compressed Free Cash Flow to -₹1.95 per ₹100 before M&A.

web_blocks.html: Between FY26 and H1 FY27, operating margins shifted from 31.2% down to ~24.0% in Q1–Q2 FY27 [3][4]. Management explicitly guided for ~24%+ EBITDA margins in FY27 for three reasons [2][3][4]. First, gRevlimid exclusivity is tapering while Mirabegron carries settlement royalties [2][7]. Second, pre-launch US commercial spend for Saroglitazar adds ~150 bps of cost ahead of March 2027 [3][5]. Third, consolidating Consumer Wellness and MedTech blends margins lower [2][3]. By FY30, management targets 28–30% consolidated EBITDA margins as specialty NCEs and biosimilars scale [4].

Vertical integration and plant redundancy also shape Zydus's cost structure. Captive API plants at Ankleshwar and Dabhasa supply key intermediates for regulated-market formulations, insulating gross margins from external shocks [2][8]. Specialized dosage sites—Moraiya for oral solids and transdermals, Ahmedabad SEZ for oncology injectables, and French facilities for Amplitude Surgical—provide multi-geography reach [8][9]. However, adding new plants and acquired intangibles raised fixed overhead. Quarterly depreciation climbed from ₹238 crore in Q4 FY25 to ₹604 crore in Q2 FY27 [1][3]. Sustaining mid-teens volume growth is therefore essential to keep operating leverage positive.

web_blocks.title: Why FY26 Cash Conversion Diverged from Record Accounting Profit
paragraphs: In FY25, Zydus converted 122% of operating profit into cash (₹6,781 Cr CFO on ₹7,058 Cr EBITDA) [1]. In FY26, CFO dropped to ₹2,117 Cr (44% CFO/EBITDA) despite ₹8,475 Cr EBITDA [1]. Two culprits explain this gap. Inventory Days jumped from 227 to 282 as Zydus built launch safety stock and absorbed Comfort Click/Amplitude inventories [1]. Zydus also funded its $120 million Mirabegron settlement with Astellas [1][7].

book_paragraphs: Walk through the unit economics of Zydus in FY26, and one number immediately jumps off the page: a 73.1% gross margin. Out of every ₹100 the company billed in FY26—₹27,148 crore in total—only ₹26.86 went to raw materials and active ingredients. That high gross margin is the hallmark of a formulation-led business rather than a commodity chemical maker. From the remaining ₹73.14, Zydus paid ₹16.27 to its scientists, plant operators, and medical reps, and spent ₹25.64 on other operating costs—which notably included ₹8.37 per ₹100 plowed straight back into R&D (₹2,273 crore in total).

That left ₹31.22 of Operating EBITDA per ₹100 of revenue, a historic high-water mark for the company. After deducting ₹5.19 for depreciation and ₹1.62 for interest, pre-tax profit stood at ₹24.39 and reported net profit at ₹18.87. On paper, those look like software-grade economics. Yet when you follow the cash down to the bottom of the waterfall, you hit a sharp reality check: Cash Flow from Operations fell to just ₹7.80 per ₹100 of revenue (₹2,117 crore), and after ₹9.75 of organic capital expenditure, Free Cash Flow turned slightly negative at -₹530 crore—before even counting the ₹5,248 crore spent on acquisitions.

Why did ₹5,124 crore of accounting profit yield only ₹2,117 crore of operating cash? Three reasons explain the gap. First, inventory days ballooned from 227 days in FY25 to 282 days in FY26 as Zydus built safety stock for new launches and absorbed newly acquired European and UK inventories. Second, Zydus booked and funded its $120 million litigation settlement with Astellas on Mirabegron. Third, as CFO Tushar Shroff and Head of IR Arvind Bothra emphasized on recent calls, Zydus is deliberately front-loading commercial spending: 'Our operating profitability remained robust with an EBITDA margin of 24% despite continued investments towards launch-related activities.'

You and I should read that 24% H1 FY27 margin not as a broken business, but as an investment-phase reset. When gRevlimid's transient windfall fades and Zydus spends 150 basis points of margin building a US hepatology sales force for Saroglitazar before a single dollar of US Saroglitazar revenue hits the P&L, near-term margins naturally compress. The real test of the plumbing over FY27–FY29 is whether gross margins hold near 70% while inventory days normalize back toward 200 days.

In pharmaceuticals, gross margin is only half the unit-economics story; the other half lives in working capital, regulatory compliance, and distribution reach. Zydus's cost of materials consumed in fiscal 2026 was just seven thousand two hundred ninety-three crore rupees on twenty-seven thousand one hundred forty-eight crore of revenue—a remarkably lean twenty-six point nine percent raw-material cost. Employee benefits consumed another four thousand four hundred eighteen crore rupees, or sixteen point three percent, reflecting both a large Indian field force and specialized research scientists.

Where Zydus's unit economics face friction is in the working-capital pipeline required to feed forty-four percent North America revenue and newly acquired international businesses. Inventory days stretched to two hundred eighty-two in fiscal 2026 as the company built safety stocks for complex US launches, absorbed Amplitude Surgical's orthopedic instrument kits, and integrated Comfort Click's European e-commerce fulfillment. Every extra week of inventory ties up cash that could otherwise pay down the thirteen thousand nine hundred sixty-six crore rupees of gross debt.

At the plant level, vertical integration into active pharmaceutical ingredients—while only two percent of external sales—acts as an internal supply-chain shock absorber, insulating key formulations from Chinese intermediate disruptions. Yet that manufacturing footprint also carries concentration risk: Moraiya and Baddi remain critical US supply nodes, meaning clean cGMP execution is the single most important operational variable in the supply chain.

Tracing a rupee of Zydus revenue through the income statement and balance sheet highlights why operational execution matters just as much as scientific discovery. Out of every hundred rupees of sales in fiscal 2026, roughly twenty-seven rupees went to raw materials and active ingredients, sixteen rupees went to employees across factories, labs, and sales territories, and eight rupees and forty paise went straight into research and development. That left thirty-one rupees and twenty paise in operating profit before depreciation, interest, and taxes.

However, between operating profit and free cash flow sits the working-capital bridge. In fiscal 2026, inventory days climbed to two hundred eighty-two and cash flow from operations dropped to forty-four percent of EBITDA. Part of that surge reflects deliberate inventory build for complex launches and newly consolidated acquisitions like Amplitude Surgical and Comfort Click. Over the next eight quarters, management's ability to release cash from those two hundred eighty-two days of inventory without disrupting US supply commitments will determine how rapidly Zydus deleverages.

Operational discipline over the coming eight quarters will hinge on two levers: normalizing the two-hundred-eighty-two-day inventory cycle built up during recent acquisitions and complex US launches, and maintaining flawless quality compliance across Moraiya, Baddi, and the newly integrated European and American facilities.

book_subsections.title: Backward Integration & Manufacturing Footprint
paragraphs: Zydus's API plants at Ankleshwar and Dabhasa provide captive active-ingredient supply for its high-volume US and emerging-market formulations, insulating gross margins from Chinese intermediate shocks. Meanwhile, specialized dosage plants—Moraiya for oral solids and transdermals, Ahmedabad SEZ for oncology injectables, and newly acquired French facilities for Amplitude Surgical—give the group multi-geography redundancy.

Even so, multi-site complexity raises fixed overhead. Quarterly depreciation rose from ₹238 crore in Q4 FY25 to ₹604 crore in Q2 FY27, meaning Zydus must sustain high-teens volume growth to keep operating leverage working in its favor.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Never confuse a 31% peak-exclusivity EBITDA margin with a permanent steady state, and never confuse a 24% pre-launch investment margin with structural decay. Separate gross margin durability (~73%) from temporary SG&A and working-capital swings.
